title: Shallow Equality Comparator (shallowEqual)
problemStatement: Implement `shallowEqual(objA, objB)` matching the exact comparator used by `React.memo` and `PureComponent`. Returns `true` if all own keys are shallowly equal using `Object.is`.
interviewTrap: Using `===` instead of `Object.is` causes `+0` and `-0` to match incorrectly and `NaN === NaN` to fail.

testCases.name: Returns true for objects with identical top-level properties
testCases.testFn: return shallowEqual({ a: 1, b: 'x' }, { a: 1, b: 'x' });

testCases.name: Returns false when nested object references differ
Handles NaN properly via Object.is
testCases.testFn: return shallowEqual({ n: NaN }, { n: NaN });

details.name: Returns true for objects with identical top-level properties

detailedExplanation.conceptualOverview: By default, when a parent component renders, all its child components re-render recursively regardless of whether their props changed. `React.memo` bails out only if all props are shallowly equal.
stepByStepWalkthrough: 1. Initialize execution context and environment records for Object & Prop Identity Comparison (Object.is).
2. Execute logic adhering to ECMAScript standard specification.
3. Verify invariant boundaries and edge conditions.
detailedExplanation.underlyingEngineInternals: In JavaScript engines (e.g. V8), Object & Prop Identity Comparison (Object.is) is optimized via inline caches, heap contexts, and bytecode translation.
edgeCasesHandled: Using `===` instead of `Object.is` causes `+0` and `-0` to match incorrectly and `NaN === NaN` to fail.

verifiedRules: Adheres to ECMAScript runtime evaluation specifications.
